about: The canonical Beads Permission rules for use-bd, for bd 1.3.0. Each of deny, ask, and allow is a list of groups; a group gives its rows outright (rows), or a list of verbs and the shapes each verb fills in for {v} (verbs, shapes). Expanded, the groups are rows for a repo's .claude/settings.json: a repo carries every canonical row and may add its own. Rule grammar: deny beats ask beats allow; * matches anywhere; a trailing space-star also matches the bare command.

deny.why: Agents touch Beads only through bdw, so the raw names Homebrew links (bd and beads) are denied outright, reads included: the habit of typing bd fails at once instead of working for reads and prompting for writes.
Invocation by install path, which a bare-name rule cannot see. Kept to the install locations so reading the wrapper's source is not denied.

Never run by an agent: irreversible, off the machine, or falsifying the record. Each verb gets the verb-first spelling (which also matches the bare call) and the flag-first spelling that catches global flags placed before the verb.

Aliases (done for close, hb for heartbeat, new for create) and link (shorthand for dep add) are denied so the use-bd Skill's one spelling of each operation is the only one, while bdw does not map them.
Closes epics because their children closed, skipping the Branch Issue's verifying pass.
Memories stay in the harness's own memory files, never in Beads; bd prime injects them even with a custom PRIME.md.

The lease reaper reverts every claim whose lease has expired to open. A lapsed lease is inert until reclaim runs, and sessions sit for hours waiting on a human, so a reclaim would rob live work. Denied rather than asked for.
Verbs that act with no arguments at all get an exact bare row as well, so the deny does not depend on the space-star-matches-bare rule.
Flags that claim the next Issue for the agent, around the choice of what to work on. Denied wherever they appear on their verb.
bd's own --actor flag would let a caller name the Actor, defeating bdw's rule that identity comes from the environment. Denied in first position and after anything.

ask.why: Flags that delete, override another Actor's claim, write files, or send data off the machine.
Close Issues on the agent's behalf. human respond comments, then closes the Issue at once; a review never closes this way, so only a human-attended call may.
Configuration, backup, and bulk changes. backup sync pushes the whole database to the backup destination.

allow.why: Reads. metrics off is the one write here: it only turns telemetry off.
Reversible writes through bdw, which carries the Actor.
Work waiting on a human is blocked by a gate; gate check closes the gates whose condition holds (a merged PR). gate resolve has no rule, so it prompts: resolving a human gate is the human's act.
Reversible, visible record-keeping: when to use them is a filing discipline (use-bd), not a permission.
